title: LivingAgentKernel — first real consumer wiring (PersistentAgent wake)
isolation: ONLY this worktree was edited. /Users/dhyana/dharma_swarm and the other ~34 persistent_agent.py copies are untouched (grep for the flag in main returns 0). No push performed. No network/provider/payment/launchctl.
goal: A real dharma_swarm PersistentAgent's wake cycle, when an OFF-by-default flag is enabled, routes through the LivingAgentKernel so the wake is governed (authority evaluated) and a tamper-evident kernel receipt is written per wake — while the agent still completes its normal task. Flag OFF = byte-identical current behavior.

flag.name: DHARMA_PERSISTENT_KERNEL_GOVERNANCE
flag.default: OFF (unset / any value not in the truthy set)
flag.idiom_reused: Mirrors the existing DHARMA_OPERATOR_BRIEF_ENABLED env-flag idiom (cron_runner.py:743) and the broader os.environ.get('DHARMA_*', default-off) pattern (DHARMA_EVOLUTION_SHADOW, DHARMA_SELF_IMPROVE, JIKOKU_ENABLED). NO new config system was invented.
flag.how_to_enable: Set the environment variable in the process that runs the persistent agent daemon, e.g. `export DHARMA_PERSISTENT_KERNEL_GOVERNANCE=1` before launching the daemon/run_loop. Unset (or set to 0/false/no/off) to disable.

injection_point.wake_method: async def wake(self, injected_task: str | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]  (the 10-step conductor heartbeat)
injection_point.sole_caller: run_loop self-wake at persistent_agent.py:569 — `await self.wake(injected_task=injected)` (return value discarded). Verified: the ONLY caller of wake() in the repo.
injection_point.where: Step 8b — inserted AFTER step 8 (the agent's own ReAct execution: `agent_result = await self._agent.wake(task_text)`) and BEFORE step 9 (save learnings).
new_symbols: _persistent_kernel_governance_enabled() — module-level flag helper, zero existing callers
PersistentAgent._govern_wake_via_kernel(task_text) — best-effort private method, zero existing callers
injection_point.diff_shape: +73 lines, 0 deletions, single source file (dharma_swarm/persistent_agent.py). Purely additive: `import os`, the flag helper, a flag-gated `if` block inside wake(), and the new private method. ZERO existing runtime lines modified or removed.
injection_point.seam_reused_verbatim: build_persistent_wake_payload(self, task=task_text)  ->  kernel.normalize_wake_source('persistent_self_wake', payload)  ->  kernel.wake(envelope, lease_owner=self.name)  ->  kernel.closeback_source_wake(execution.wake_record, result, source_root=self.state_dir). KernelRunStore is rooted at self.state_dir/living_agent_kernel.
injection_point.observe_plus_govern: The agent's own task ALWAYS runs first (step 8) and is never replaced. Governance is best-effort: the ENTIRE _govern_wake_via_kernel body (including the lazy imports) is wrapped in `try/except Exception -> return None`, so a flag-ON wake can never break the agent. When ON it adds optional keys (kernel_governed / kernel_run_id / kernel_status) to the returned result_info; the run_loop caller discards that dict, so the contract change is invisible to consumers.
injection_point.off_path: When the env var is unset the gate is False, step 8b is skipped entirely, no kernel modules are imported (lazy imports live inside the gated method), and result_info gains no kernel_* keys. ~313ns short-circuit cost per wake at the 1800s interval — negligible.

activation_steps: 1. MERGE / PORT THE WIRING. The consumer wiring lives ONLY in the isolated worktree /Users/dhyana/dharma_swarm_lak_e2e (branch lak-e2e, commits f6eee080f + 32fa22c5e). To make a live production agent use it, port the additive change into the worktree that actually runs your persistent-agent daemon (e.g. /Users/dhyana/dharma_swarm). CRITICAL: that change depends on the LivingAgentKernel seam modules — dharma_swarm/operator_core/living_agent_kernel.py and living_agent_kernel_persistent_adapter.py — which currently exist ONLY in the lak-e2e worktree. You MUST bring those seam modules over in the SAME commit, otherwise flag-ON will silently no-op (the lazy ImportError is swallowed by design). Verify after porting: `export PYTHONPATH=<that-worktree> && python3 -m pytest tests/test_persistent_agent.py tests/test_living_agent_kernel_persistent_integration.py -q` should be green (flag still OFF = byte-identical).

2. SET THE FLAG ON THE DAEMON PROCESS. In the environment that launches the persistent-agent run_loop, set: `export DHARMA_PERSISTENT_KERNEL_GOVERNANCE=1` (truthy = 1/true/yes/on; anything else = OFF). Then start/restart the daemon. From that point, every PersistentAgent.wake() (self-wake from run_loop:569) routes through the kernel: authority is evaluated and a tamper-evident receipt (proof_ledger.jsonl + wake_ledger.jsonl + a self-wake witness receipt) is written per wake under that agent's own state_dir/living_agent_kernel, while the agent still completes its normal task. To turn it back off: `unset DHARMA_PERSISTENT_KERNEL_GOVERNANCE` (or set to 0) and restart — behavior reverts to byte-identical current.
honest_state: SAFE to enable in this isolated worktree (lak-e2e) as-is: flag-OFF is proven byte-identical (additive-only diff, zero modified runtime lines, 17/72/239 passed across suites), and flag-ON is proven to GOVERN a real wake while the agent still completes its task — durable, tamper-evident, replay-verified receipts under the agent's own state_dir, with two decorrelated PASS reviews. PROVEN: (a) flag OFF = no-op (no import, no key, no dir, ~313ns gate); (b) flag ON governs the REAL wake() hot-path (kernel seam not monkeypatched; only the step-8 LLM ReAct call stubbed to avoid a provider hit); (c) authority is actually evaluated and changes the receipt (forced 'block' flips kernel_status to blocked); (d) receipts are tamper-evident (hash-chain independently recomputed from disk; tamper breaks the chain) and replay-verifiable; (e) observe+govern only — the agent's own task always runs first and is never replaced, and all kernel exceptions are swallowed so flag-ON cannot break the wake. NOT YET PROVEN / CAVEATS: (1) Live provider smoke — the flag-ON test stubs the LLM call (no network), so the seam has not run against a real live provider response under flag-ON; the OFF path is fully live. (2) Worktree drift — the wiring + seam exist only in lak-e2e; ~34 other persistent_agent.py copies (including /Users/dhyana/dharma_swarm) do not have it. Default-OFF makes this safe to defer, but step-1 porting MUST carry the seam modules too or flag-ON silently no-ops. (3) Per-wake cost when ON — each governed wake constructs a fresh LivingAgentKernel and writes 3 durable ledger files (real disk I/O); negligible at the 1800s wake interval but real. (4) Authority default is read-only/manual — a flag-ON wake whose payload requested apply_patch would be DENIED+recorded; the agent's own task already executed independently in step 8, so this only affects the receipt, never the agent's work. (5) Cross-host coordination is out of scope — kernel lease atomicity is single-machine (service flock, local-FS only). Bottom line: safe to enable; the one thing an operator should do before trusting it in production is a single live-provider flag-ON smoke run under approved budget to confirm a real LLM response also produces a clean governed receipt.
headline: First real consumer wired: a live PersistentAgent's self-wake now routes through LivingAgentKernel under the OFF-by-default env flag DHARMA_PERSISTENT_KERNEL_GOVERNANCE — flag OFF is byte-identical (17/72/239 passed), flag ON governs the real wake and writes a tamper-evident, replay-verified per-wake receipt while the agent still completes its task; two decorrelated reviewers PASS; isolated to lak-e2e, no push, main untouched.
